verdictRationale: The pending-object split and refuse-at-release trilemma are the right diagnosis of observation A, but the proposed custody envelope charges regenerable rungs (12 × 64 MiB helper ceiling) and 4 KiB once-view floors, which can make a single legal asset undeletable; reset is gated on an uncapped live set; E_ASSET_CAPACITY in family assets with structured fields and HTTP 422 cannot be implemented on ExecutionState.Rejected, jobs::rejection_family, and upload_refusal_status as they exist at the 0.0.10/current pin. A simpler complete design keeps a finite original-payload bound and 24h original grace without those terms.

established: 40 successful deletes charge 40 unlocated ready rows / 6204 payload bytes and block a zero-usage principal at upload HTTP 422 (after-40-releases-database.json charged.objects=40 charged.bytes=6204; assets_ledger.rs:247-259,214-232).
Usage predicate is unlocated receiving OR (ready AND reclaiming=0); claimed locators are excluded; ready tombstones and failed rows leave the query (assets_ledger.rs:247-259,378-388,428-445).
Limits 20/40 objects and 256/512 MiB are STAGING_* constants; enforce_staging_caps is not called from reconcile_row_assets (assets_ledger.rs:14-17,542-616).
158-byte dedup blobs have st_blocks=8 (4096 allocated) and the stopped SQLite header page size is 4096; logical 4 KiB floor is a fixture observation, not total disk.
IMAGE_WIDTH_RUNGS has 12 entries; MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES is 64 MiB; MAX_HTTP_WORKERS=64; MAX_UPLOAD_WORKERS=4; MAX_MEDIA_HELPERS=2; ASSET_SWEEP_INTERVAL=60s; ASSET_RECLAIM_GRACE_MS=86400000.
Replay stores rejected terminals; conflict precedes program rejection (replay.rs:156-164; LLP 1012 §7). Grant lifetime 30 days vs asset grace 24h.
conjecture: Ordinary edit rate, typical rung byte sizes, and whether a production store would hit C(i) > envelope from originals alone.
How often once-delivery races release; the 64-worker standing tax is sized for that race, not measured.

findings.title: Release-gating envelope includes regenerable rungs and view floors, creating individually undeletable assets within published ceilings
findings.design: policy-design.md §4 C(i)=payload+V+H*(2+K+W), K≤12; §4 explicit compatibility: a single live asset with large derived data or view history can exceed the transfer budget and waiting cannot help.

source.note: IMAGE_WIDTH_RUNGS length 12
MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES = 64 MiB per encoded rung
record_asset_view does not check locator; delivery_row refuses unlocated ids

findings.evidence: 12 rungs × 64 MiB plus original exceeds 512 MiB − 262144 using only published constants. Guest mint is free (LLP 1006 §4), so W(i) is unbounded per once-image. While claimed, V and W are outside C; release is the first fit check; locators then cannot clear and rungs cannot GC.
findings.conjecture: How often real photos approach the 64 MiB rung ceiling. The legal maximum is not conjecture.
findings.whyNotPredicateTweak: Excluding released_at from the current query would leave an unbounded grace pool; that option stays rejected. The defect is what is summed into C, not the existence of a finite C.
findings.resolution: Charge only original max(staged, finalized) plus failed/reclaiming originals until finish. Delete or refuse to publish {id}.w* when unlocated. Keep _asset_views for once-across-reclaim; do not put W(i)*H in C. Refuse release only when original payload does not fit. Drop 12-slot ledger, standing 256 KiB view margin, and rung-reservation protocol.

findings.title: Reset-gated-on-C refuses existing grace-waiving teardown for any live set larger than the garbage envelope
findings.design: policy-design.md §6: explicit reset that would transfer more than custody capacity must not silently create an oversized garbage backlog; refuse before clearing rows. Large reset called a root compatibility cost.

source.note: reset clears staging, clear_assets, then sweep_asset_blobs in one owner action
clear_assets marks every row reclaiming and clears locators; no 24h wait
§9a reset clears live _assets and staging then ordinary sweep; does not empty blobs a fork still references

findings.evidence: Live application storage is explicitly uncapped by this policy. Reset already waives 24h. Requiring the live set to fit in 512 MiB garbage blocks reset of any successful media app. Observation A does not involve reset.
findings.resolution: Keep current reset teardown. Charge only ids whose physical delete failed. Do not treat live→tombstone as a 24h grace transfer that must fit C.

findings.title: E_ASSET_CAPACITY diagnostic contract does not fit actual rejection carriers
findings.design: policy-design.md §8: family assets, structured pool/scope/resource/delta/usage/limit/phase, HTTP 422 on upload, HTTP 200 rejected on mutation/replay, do not parse strings; carry detail through writer_wire.rs and offline.rs::replay_mutation_response.

source.note: execute_certified maps mutation_rejection_code errors to ExecutionState::Rejected { code, message: error.to_string() } only
hardcoded rewrite 'fix the rejected mutation input and retry'; family via writer_util
rejection_family delegates to snapback2_core::jobs::rejection_family, not a local table
JobRefusal::rejected and rejection_family; unknown E_* → family input
third family mapper, same input default; hardcoded rewrite
AssetTooLarge special-cased to family input; AssetViewed to assets
upload_refusal_status is 422 only if E_ASSET_* AND family == input; family assets → HTTP 400
mutation_rejection_code already maps AssetTooLarge/AssetInUse; a new variant must be added here or execute_certified emits Refusal

findings.evidence: Three family mappers; Rejected is two strings; upload 422 is gated on family input. Design names writer_wire.rs and offline.rs but the mutation JSON family comes from jobs.rs.
findings.resolution: Specify a structured carrier on Execution/Rejected (not packed into message). Patch jobs::rejection_family, offline.rs copy, Refusal::from_runtime, upload_refusal_status, execute_certified, and JobRefusal::rejected together. Keep E_ASSET_TOO_LARGE for column/helper size only.

findings.title: 64-worker late-view margin and 12-slot rung accounting are complexity required only by F1
findings.design: policy-design.md §4 reserve 64×H=262144 in each envelope; §6 items 1 and 3 add 12 derived-width slots and view-count scalar; GC must skip MediaJobs guards.

source.note: MAX_HTTP_WORKERS=64; asset GET is Json; JSON may occupy 60 non-control slots
ensure_rung/render_rung put without ledger reservation or locator re-check
deletes blobs for reclaimed_ids even if id still in live _assets; no MediaJobs interaction

findings.evidence: 64 is conservative vs 60 Json workers. Standing 256 KiB tax applies even when no once-delivery is in flight. Rung/GC races are unhandled today and become new writer protocol if unlocated rungs stay charged.
findings.resolution: If F1 is adopted, delete the margin, view scalar, and rung slots. If rungs remain in C, the race table is required work, not an optional test.

findings.title: Failed-unlink scratch can still mint unbounded unique temps under current allocate_path
findings.design: policy-design.md §6 item 5: retain every temporary until unlink succeeds; do not recycle the physical-work slot; do not claim a bounded scratch pool while failed unlinks create fresh untracked files.

source.note: allocate_path always new name; boot sweep deletes matching prefixes or refuses startup
HEIC normalize and render_rung allocate_path/create_named without failed-path slot retention

findings.evidence: Each retry currently chooses a new {label}-{hex}-{seq}.stage. Boot sweep is bounded cleanup, not live-slot retention.
findings.resolution: Keep this part of the design. It is independent of F1 and is real disk-unboundedness, separate from 512 MiB logical C. Do not relabel scratch as inside the garbage envelope (design already does not).

findings.title: Net custody check insertion point is correct; job/migration/operator/reset paths must be named as distinct carriers
findings.design: policy-design.md §5: validate net custody in attempted result path ahead of replay::finish_run; same final check on successors, jobs/chunks, operator mutations, reset.

source.note: constraints/bounds then replay finish_run; ordinary mutation Err at 761 converted later by execute_certified; reset_and_execute is a separate transaction that already called clear_assets
assert_bounds then save cursor and commit; no execute_certified wrapper
chunk Err parks via JobRefusal::rejected; already-committed chunks remain
apply_migration_drops releases table/column assets with no capacity check
reconciler releases then claims; intermediate C can exceed final C

findings.evidence: Net-final is required because of release-then-claim order. Replay conflict precedence already exists and must remain. Jobs park on Err; that is acceptable if the parked envelope is the same structured capacity refusal.
findings.resolution: Keep net-final-before-settle. Name execute_certified, run_chunk park, apply_migration_drops, and reset_and_execute as four call sites with their existing rollback/park/commit behavior. Reset site should follow F2, not F1's refuse-before-clear.

findings.title: Upgrade grandfather and unknown-size reconstruction are underspecified
findings.design: policy-design.md §9: do not backfill missing sizes as zero; transition bound max(measured pre-upgrade custody, new bound); non-increasing until restored; no two versions write one store.

source.note: _assets has no rung-size or view-count columns; ensure_column is the existing additive path
rung keys are {id}.w{width}

findings.evidence: 40-release fixture C under the published formula is 333884 bytes, not over-capacity. Old payload-only query omitted failed/reclaiming and overhead, so other stores can be over after reconstruction.
findings.resolution: State that max(measured, new) is an open/status ceiling, not a growth target; operative rule is non-increasing while measured > new. Unreadable original: owner I/O, no positive allocation. Absent original: do not invent 0 if the row still exists as ready; treat as GC-missing only after tombstone semantics. If F1 drops rung charges, do not backfill V from enumerate.

findings.title: Operator-visible saturation paths: fork pins and cross-creator delete
findings.design: policy-design.md §4 fork/snapshot storage; §5 do not charge the actor who deletes another creator's row; §8 operator copy for owner pressure.

2026-09-05 move deleted the fork CLI adapter

findings.evidence: No public creator operation deletes another creator's grace or a fork file. Operator seat can still fail a delete that overflows the uploader's C.
findings.resolution: Operator guide must say: leftover .snapback/forks/*.sqlite pins cleanup charges; deleting a row charges the uploader's envelope, not the actor's; waiting does not help if required > limit.

simplerCompleteDesign.stillFinite: Unlocated original payload plus unfinished failed deletes cannot grow past 256/512 MiB; unlocated identity count remains bounded if a row cap or small per-id unit is kept. Live application storage stays uncapped. Regenerable rungs of unlocated ids are deleted without waiting 24h and are not a garbage pool.
simplerCompleteDesign.doesNotWaiveGrace: Ordinary unclaimed originals still get 86,400,000 ms. Reset already waives grace in 0.0.10; this revision does not newly waive it for deletes/replacements.

remainingRootDecisionsAfterRevision: Accept refuse-at-release when original unlocated payload would exceed 256/512 MiB (full grace + finite garbage; not unlimited successful release).
Do not reserve live-set deletion space at first claim.
Leave server asset TTL at 24h while offline intent/grant lifetime remains up to 30 days.
